title: Settings screen
prompt: Design the Notifications settings page of "Ledgerly", a bookkeeping web app for small agencies. Desktop, 1280x832, light theme. Layout: app sidebar (Dashboard, Invoices, Expenses, Reports, Settings active), a settings sub-navigation (Profile, Workspace, Members, Billing, Notifications active, Integrations), and the Notifications panel. The panel has: a page title and short description; an "Email" group with 4 toggles (Invoice paid - on, Invoice overdue - on, Weekly summary - off, Product updates - off) each with a one-line description; a "Delivery" group with a select for digest frequency (Daily at 9:00 AM) and a radio group for quiet hours (Off / 8 PM - 7 AM selected / Custom); and a footer bar with "Cancel" and a primary "Save changes" button, plus an unsaved-changes hint "You have 2 unsaved changes". Dense but calm, like a well-made admin tool.
requiredContent: Email group with 4 toggles in the stated on/off states, each with a description
Digest frequency select showing Daily at 9:00 AM
Quiet hours radio group with 8 PM - 7 AM selected

checklist.text: Both navigation levels are present and Settings / Notifications are visibly active.
Exactly four email toggles; Invoice paid and Invoice overdue are on, Weekly summary and Product updates are off, and on/off states are unambiguous.
Each toggle row has a label and a one-line description, and the toggle controls align on one vertical edge.
The digest select shows "Daily at 9:00 AM" and looks like a select (chevron or similar).
The quiet hours radio group has three options with "8 PM - 7 AM" selected.
"Save changes" is the only primary-styled button; Cancel is secondary.
The unsaved-changes hint is present near the action buttons.
Groups are separated by consistent spacing or dividers, with group headings.
Labels, descriptions and controls use a consistent type scale (no more than ~4 distinct text sizes in the panel).
No text is clipped, overlapping, or overflowing.
Description text is readable (>= 12px, sufficient contrast).
